title: Patriarchs to the First Kings
intro: Canaan is a land of fortified city-states between Egypt and Mesopotamia. The Bible’s accounts of the Patriarchs, the Exodus and the conquest are traditional, and their dates are approximate. The first outside mention of Israel comes from Egypt.
tp: The Middle Bronze Age begins. Fortified cities rise across the land and Canaanite worship of Baal, Asherah and El takes shape.
Biblical tradition places Abraham’s journey to Canaan in these years, with family-based worship.
Pharaoh Merneptah’s victory stele mentions Israel as a people. It is the earliest known mention outside the Bible.
Canaanite city-states fall. The Sea Peoples arrive, among them the Philistines, and Shiloh and Shechem become religious centers.
Philistine city-states form on the coastal plain while early Israelite villages appear in the hills.
Under Philistine pressure the tribes accept a king. Saul is the first.
also: Hazor becomes a great city. It is the largest fortified city in the region, a hub on the trade road between Egypt and Mesopotamia.
The Battle of Kadesh. Ramses II of Egypt and the Hittites fight for control of the Levant.
Fortified cities such as Jericho and Arad are founded.
Isaac and Jacob, and Joseph’s rise in Egypt, by tradition. The Hyksos bring chariots.
The Hyksos are expelled from Egypt. Thutmose III takes Megiddo and Egypt rules Canaan.
The Amarna letters show unrest. Hazor, Lachish and Gezer stay loyal to Egypt.
Traditional date of Joshua’s conquest. Worship gathers around Yahweh.
Deborah and Barak defeat a Canaanite army, by tradition.
The Ark of the Covenant is kept at Shiloh.
Philistine pressure on the tribes grows.
David defeats Goliath and begins his rise, by tradition.
Hyksos rulers of Canaanite origin take power in Egypt.
Ramses III defeats the Sea Peoples in battles on Egypt’s coast.
The earliest alphabetic inscriptions are cut by Canaanite workers at Serabit el-Khadim in Sinai.
The Song of Deborah is composed. Its date is debated and it may be among the oldest texts of the Bible.
The Phoenician alphabet, ancestor of the Hebrew, Greek and Latin letters, takes shape.
The Psalms are attributed by tradition to David.

title: Kings and Prophets
intro: David makes Jerusalem the capital and Solomon builds the First Temple. The kingdom then splits in two. The prophets speak out against kings and idols, Assyria ends the north, and Babylon ends the south.
tp: He unites the tribes into one kingdom and secures the trade routes.
The kingdom reaches its height in wealth and trade, and Jerusalem becomes a religious center.
After Solomon’s death the northern tribes form Israel and the south becomes Judah.
Ahab of Israel joins an alliance that fights Assyria. It is the first Assyrian record that names an Israelite king.
The northern kingdom is conquered and its people are scattered.
The Assyrian king besieges Jerusalem and does not take it. Hezekiah’s water tunnel supplies the city.
A law book found during Temple repairs leads the king to end idol worship.
Jerusalem falls, the Temple is burned and Judah’s leaders are taken to Babylon.
also: The prophet Nathan rebukes King David, by tradition.
The Gezer calendar, an early Hebrew inscription, records the farming year.
Pharaoh Shishak raids Judah and Israel.
Omri founds Samaria as the capital of the northern kingdom.
Ahab and Jezebel promote the worship of Baal. The prophets Elijah and Elisha oppose it.
Jehu overthrows Ahab’s house in a coup and ends Baal worship.
The Mesha Stele of Moab tells of Israel’s rule over Moab.
The prophets Amos and Hosea condemn injustice and idolatry.
Isaiah and Micah prophesy in Judah, and Isaiah’s poetry shapes the Hebrew Bible.
Assyria takes the Galilee and sends many of its people into exile.
The Siloam inscription records the digging of Hezekiah’s tunnel.
Jeremiah begins to prophesy. After the fall, Lamentations mourns Jerusalem.
Babylon captures Jerusalem for the first time.
The Lachish letters, written in Hebrew on pottery, record Judah’s last days.

title: Exile and Return
intro: The exiles keep their faith by the rivers of Babylon. Persia conquers Babylon and lets them go home. They rebuild the Temple and the walls of Jerusalem, and the Torah becomes the law of the people.
tp: Judah’s leaders and craftsmen are taken to Babylon.
The governor appointed by Babylon is killed, and many Judeans flee to Egypt.
The Persian king conquers Babylon and allows the Jews to go home and rebuild.
It stands on the site of the first, in the Persian province of Yehud.
He teaches the Torah and leads a renewal of the covenant.
A governor sent by the Persian king restores the walls of Jerusalem, by tradition in 52 days.
Scribes under Persian rule gather the Torah, the prophets and the histories.
Alexander the Great conquers the land.
Persian rule ends and Greek rule begins.
also: Ezekiel prophesies among the exiles in Babylon.
Darius I takes the Persian throne and confirms the right to rebuild the Temple.
Egypt breaks away from Persia, and Judea becomes a border province.
Alexander defeats Darius III at Issus.
The Babylonians leave the poorest of the land to work its vineyards and fields.
King Jehoiachin of Judah is released from prison in Babylon.
The prophecies of comfort in the later chapters of Isaiah console the exiles.
The first exiles return under Sheshbazzar.
The prophets Haggai and Zechariah urge the rebuilding of the Temple.
Zerubbabel, of the house of David, governs Judea.
The story of Esther is set at the Persian court of Xerxes.
The Samaritans build a temple on Mount Gerizim, according to excavations.
Malachi, the last of the prophets, preaches in Jerusalem.
Jews of Elephantine in Egypt write to the governor of Judea to rebuild their temple.
Silver coins stamped Yehud are minted in Judea.
A Jewish revolt against Persia is put down.

title: Greeks, Hasmoneans and Romans
intro: Alexander brings Greek rule and Greek culture. A revolt against Greek rule creates the Hasmonean kingdom. Rome takes over, Herod rebuilds Jerusalem, and in 70 the Romans destroy the Second Temple.
tp: Alexander the Great conquers the land.
Greek culture and Greek-style cities arrive with him.
Antiochus IV desecrates the Temple and bans Jewish practice. Judah Maccabee leads the revolt.
The Maccabees retake Jerusalem. The rededication is the first Hanukkah.
Simon is confirmed as ruler and high priest, and Judea is independent.
Judea becomes a client state of Rome.
Rome’s client king launches huge building projects, among them the rebuilding of the Temple.
Heavy taxes and religious tension set off a rebellion.
The Romans destroy the Second Temple.
Titus takes Jerusalem and burns the Temple. Masada falls in 73.
also: Antiochus III takes Judea. The Seleucid king defeats the Ptolemies at Panium and Seleucid rule begins.
Aristobulus I takes the title of king. He is the first Hasmonean ruler to do so.
Pontius Pilate becomes governor of Judea. He governs for about ten years.
Jesus is crucified in Jerusalem. The event is the foundation of Christianity.
A Jewish revolt against Persia is put down.
The Ptolemies of Egypt take control of the land.
The Seleucids win control after the Battle of Gaza. The two dynasties keep fighting for the land.
The Septuagint, a Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible, is begun in Alexandria.
Antiochus IV takes the Seleucid throne and presses Hellenization.
Judah Maccabee dies and his brothers Jonathan and Simon lead.
Alexander Jannaeus rules as king and expands the kingdom further.
Queen Salome Alexandra rules in relative peace.
Herod begins the great renovation of the Temple. 4 BCE Herod dies and his kingdom is divided among his sons. 6 CE Judea becomes a Roman province under a governor.
Scholars at Yavne reorganize Jewish practice without the Temple.
The core of the Hebrew Bible reaches its settled form.
Paul begins his journeys across the Roman Empire.
Vespasian’s army begins the conquest of the Galilee.
Ben Sira writes his book of wisdom in Jerusalem.
The Qumran community gathers scrolls written from the 3rd century BCE to the 1st century CE.
Herod builds the harbor and theater of Caesarea.
Josephus writes The Jewish War in Rome.

title: Rabbinic Judaism and Roman Rule
intro: After Bar Kokhba, Jewish life gathers around the sages. The Mishnah and the Talmuds are written, and in the fourth century Roman rule becomes Byzantine Christian rule.
left: Hadrian bars the Jews from Jerusalem.
After the Bar Kokhba revolt fails, Jerusalem becomes Aelia Capitolina and Judea is renamed Syria Palaestina.
The surviving sages reconvene at Usha in the Galilee and rebuild the Sanhedrin.
Rabbi Judah the Prince writes down the oral law in the Galilee.
Beth Shearim becomes the burial place of Rabbi Judah the Prince and the sages.
Rabbi Yohanan heads the academy of Tiberias, whose teachings fill the Jerusalem Talmud.
Jews in the Galilee rise against Roman rule. Sepphoris, Tiberias and Lod are damaged as it is put down.
Hillel II publishes a fixed Hebrew calendar, according to tradition.
Julian plans to rebuild the Temple.
The emperor allows work to begin in Jerusalem. It stops within weeks, after a fire, an earthquake and his death in battle.
The Hammat Tiberias synagogue is laid with its zodiac mosaic.
It is finished in the Galilee and builds on the Mishnah.
Rome stops recognizing the Jewish patriarch in Tiberias, the head of the Jews for centuries.
Empress Eudocia allows Jews to pray at the Temple Mount on the festivals.
The sages of Babylonia finish the work that becomes the core of Jewish law.
right: Caracalla grants Roman citizenship to all free men of the empire, Jews among them.
Queen Zenobia of Palmyra seizes the eastern provinces until Rome retakes them in 272.
Constantine ends the persecution of Christians. Jerusalem soon becomes a center of Christian pilgrimage.
Constantine takes the eastern empire, and the land comes under a Christian emperor.
Empress Helena visits the Holy Land, and churches rise at Bethlehem and the Mount of Olives.
Constantinople becomes the capital of the empire.
The Church of the Holy Sepulchre is consecrated in Jerusalem.
Theodosius makes Christianity the religion of the empire.
The empire splits in two, and the land is ruled from Constantinople.
The Theodosian Code bars Jews from public office.
The Council of Chalcedon makes Jerusalem a patriarchate of the Church.
Rome falls in the West. Byzantium rules on in the East.

title: Byzantine Decline and Islamic Conquest
intro: Byzantine laws press on the Jews of the land while the academies of Babylonia lead. Persia invades, Arab armies take Jerusalem in 638, and the Umayyads rule from Damascus.
left: The Beth Alpha synagogue is built with its zodiac mosaic floor.
Mar Zutra III comes from Babylonia to head the Sanhedrin in Tiberias.
The poet Yannai writes piyyutim, Hebrew hymns for the synagogue.
The age of the Geonim begins at the academies of Babylonia.
Jews fight beside the Persians and briefly govern the city.
Emperor Heraclius retakes Jerusalem and expels the Jews.
Seventy Jewish families from Tiberias settle in Jerusalem, by tradition.
The academy of the land of Israel meets in Tiberias.
right: Justinian becomes emperor. His laws restrict Jews and Samaritans.
The Samaritans revolt against Byzantine rule and are crushed.
The Plague of Justinian strikes the land.
Justinian dedicates the Nea Church in Jerusalem.
The Madaba Map mosaic, made in these years, shows Jerusalem and the Holy Land.
The land reaches a peak of population and prosperity.
Muhammad leaves Mecca for Medina, the start of Islam.
The Arabs defeat the Byzantines at the Yarmuk River.
Caliph Umar takes Jerusalem and allows Jews to settle there again.
Muawiya founds the dynasty and rules the region from Damascus.
The Umayyads build it on the Temple Mount.
The al-Aqsa Mosque is built on the Temple Mount.
Ramla is founded as the capital of the province of Palestine.
The rules for non-Muslims later called the Pact of Umar take shape.
It ruins Tiberias, Beit Shean and other towns across the land.

title: Abbasid and Early Medieval Judaism
intro: The Abbasid caliphs rule from Baghdad, where the Geonim guide the Jews of the world. Tiberias fixes the text of the Bible, and Jerusalem passes to the Fatimids of Cairo.
left: Anan ben David founds the Karaite movement in Babylonia.
Karaite Jews, who reject the oral law, settle in Jerusalem.
They fix the vowel signs and the text of the Hebrew Bible.
The Aleppo Codex of the Bible is written in Tiberias.
Aaron ben Meir of the Jerusalem academy clashes with Saadia Gaon of Babylonia over the calendar.
Saadia Gaon heads the academy of Sura.
He translates the Bible into Arabic and writes the first great work of Jewish philosophy.
The academy of the land of Israel moves from Tiberias to Jerusalem.
Jews gather on the Mount of Olives each Hoshana Rabbah to pray and proclaim the calendar.
Letters later found in the Cairo Geniza record Jewish life in the land.
Daniel ben Azariah, of the house of David, heads the academy in Jerusalem.
The academy leaves Jerusalem for Tyre after the Seljuk conquest.
right: The capital moves from Damascus to Baghdad, and the land becomes a far province.
Ahmad ibn Tulun adds the land to his Egyptian dynasty.
The Ikhshidids rule the land from Egypt.
Rule passes to Cairo. Wars between the Fatimids and their rivals wear the land down.
The geographer al-Muqaddasi of Jerusalem describes his home province.
The Church of the Holy Sepulchre is destroyed.
Caliph al-Hakim orders it torn down and persecutes Christians and Jews.
An earthquake damages Jerusalem, Ramla and other towns.
The Church of the Holy Sepulchre is rebuilt with Byzantine help.
In 1077 they put down a revolt in the city with a massacre. The Jerusalem academy of the Jewish sages later moves to Tyre.
Pope Urban II calls the First Crusade.
The Fatimids retake Jerusalem a year before the Crusaders arrive.

title: Crusaders and Ayyubids
intro: Crusaders take Jerusalem and found a Latin kingdom. Saladin retakes the city in 1187, and Jewish learning flowers around the Mediterranean, above all in Maimonides.
left: Jews of Egypt and Ashkelon ransom captives and Torah scrolls taken in Jerusalem.
Yehuda Halevi sails for Zion after writing “My heart is in the East”.
Maimonides visits Acre, Jerusalem and Hebron.
Benjamin of Tudela tours the land and records its Jewish communities.
Petahiah of Regensburg travels through the land and visits the graves of the sages.
Maimonides completes the Guide for the Perplexed.
In Egypt he joins Jewish law and Greek philosophy.
Saladin destroys Ashkelon, and its Jews move to Jerusalem.
Scholars from France and England arrive in the “Aliyah of the 300 Rabbis”.
The poet Judah al-Harizi visits Jerusalem and finds its Jews returned.
right: Their capture is followed by the killing of Jews and Muslims and the ruin of Jewish towns.
The port becomes the gateway of the kingdom.
The Second Crusade fails at Damascus.
The rebuilt Church of the Holy Sepulchre is consecrated.
Saladin wins at Hattin and retakes Jerusalem.
Jews are allowed to return after decades of Crusader rule.
The Third Crusade wins back the coast, and Acre becomes the Crusader capital.
Richard and Saladin sign a truce. Christian pilgrims may visit Jerusalem.
The Ayyubid ruler tears down the walls of Jerusalem.
Frederick II regains Jerusalem by treaty.
The emperor wins the city from the sultan of Egypt without a battle.
The city is lost to the Crusaders for good.
The Mamluks seize power in Egypt.

title: Mamluk Rule and the Spanish Expulsion
intro: The Mamluk sultans of Egypt drive out the last Crusaders and rule the land as a province. In Europe Jews face expulsions, and Spain expels its Jews in 1492.
left: Rabbi Yehiel of Paris settles in Acre with his students.
The great scholar re-establishes the Jewish community and opens a synagogue.
Rabbi Meir of Rothenburg is seized while setting out for the land of Israel.
Ishtori Haparchi completes Kaftor va-Ferach, the first Hebrew geography of the land.
The Ramban Synagogue moves to its site in the Jewish Quarter.
Jews and Franciscans clash over David’s Tomb on Mount Zion.
Jews of Jerusalem rebuild it the next year.
Meshullam of Volterra travels through the land and writes an account.
Rabbi Ovadiah of Bertinoro arrives in Jerusalem.
Many settle in Ottoman lands, among them Safed and Jerusalem.
Portugal forces its Jews to convert.
right: The Mamluks defeat the Mongols at Ain Jalut.
The Mamluks of Egypt take over the land.
Baybars takes Caesarea and Arsuf from the Crusaders.
Sultan Baybars takes Safed from the Templars.
Acre and the other ports are torn down so that the Crusaders cannot return.
Safed becomes the capital of a Mamluk province in the Galilee.
The Cotton Merchants’ Market is built in Jerusalem.
The plague kills much of the population of the land.
Sultan Qaitbay builds his fountain on the Temple Mount.
Mujir al-Din writes his history of Jerusalem and Hebron.
The Ottomans defeat the Mamluks at Marj Dabiq.

title: Ottoman Rule and Jewish Resettlement
intro: The Ottomans take the land in 1516 and 1517. Safed becomes the center of Jewish mysticism and law, and Sephardi and later Hasidic Jews settle in the holy cities.
left: Exiles from Spain strengthen the Jewish community of Hebron.
Joseph Nasi wins a grant of Tiberias from the sultan and plans a Jewish refuge.
Joseph Karo publishes the Shulchan Aruch.
The code of Jewish law is written in Safed.
His teaching makes Safed the center of Kabbalah.
The first printing press in the land opens in Safed.
The Ottoman governor closes the Ramban Synagogue.
Rabbi Isaiah Horowitz comes to Jerusalem from Prague.
News of the Chmielnicki massacres in Eastern Europe sends Jews to the land.
Fighting among local rulers ruins both Jewish towns.
Shabbetai Zevi is proclaimed Messiah in Gaza.
The movement sweeps the Jewish world and collapses when he converts to Islam.
Judah the Pious leads a group to Jerusalem.
He dies days after they arrive. In 1720 creditors burn their synagogue, later rebuilt as the Hurva.
Zahir al-Umar invites Rabbi Haim Abulafia to restore the Jewish community.
Rabbi Haim ibn Attar, the Or ha-Haim, founds an academy in Jerusalem.
Rabbi Gershon of Kuty, brother-in-law of the Baal Shem Tov, settles in the land.
Hasidic Jews settle in Tiberias and Safed.
right: Selim I takes Jerusalem from the Mamluks.
Suleiman builds public fountains in Jerusalem.
Suleiman rebuilds the walls of Jerusalem.
The walls still stand around the Old City.
The Haseki Sultan soup kitchen opens in Jerusalem.
The Druze emir Fakhr al-Din rules the Galilee for the Ottomans.
The Naqib al-Ashraf revolt holds Jerusalem for two years.
An earthquake damages Safed, Tiberias and Acre.
Jazzar Pasha begins his rule from Acre.
Jazzar Pasha holds the city and the French retreat to Egypt.

title: The Ottoman Land
intro: Jews, Muslims and Christians live under Ottoman and then Egyptian rule. Pilgrims, scholars and travelers arrive, and the first Jewish neighborhood rises outside the walls of Jerusalem.
tp: Muhammad Ali’s son Ibrahim Pasha conquers the land. Egyptian rule lasts until 1840 and opens it to European consuls, missionaries and travelers.
Thousands die in Safed and Tiberias, among them much of the Jewish community.
Moses Montefiore buys land outside the walls. The first Jewish neighborhood outside the Old City follows.
The German Jewish socialist argues that Jews are a nation and need a homeland in the land of Israel.
The Prussian rabbi urges Jews to buy land and farm it in the land of Israel and so begin the redemption.
Travel and trade to the land become faster and cheaper.
The agricultural school near Jaffa trains the first farmers.
The first modern Jewish farming village is founded.
also: About 7,000 Jews live in the land, mostly in four holy cities.
The Perushim, disciples of the Vilna Gaon, settle in Safed and Jerusalem.
The Perushim complete the Hurva Synagogue in Jerusalem.
Mordecai Noah of New York proposes a Jewish refuge, Ararat.
Moses Montefiore makes his first visit to the land.
An Arab revolt against Egyptian rule devastates Safed and Tiberias.
Britain opens the first consulate in Jerusalem.
The painter David Roberts tours the land, and his lithographs bring it to Europe.
The Damascus Affair shows how exposed Jews are. European powers intervene.
European powers and the Ottomans end Egyptian rule.
Britain and Prussia found a Protestant bishopric in Jerusalem.
Rabbi Yehuda Alkalai writes in support of Jewish resettlement.
Moses Montefiore visits Jerusalem and funds housing.
Abraham Mapu publishes Ahavat Zion, the first Hebrew novel, set in ancient Israel.
The Ottoman reform edict promises equality to non-Muslims.
The Ottoman Land Code reshapes land ownership.
The Alliance Israélite Universelle is founded to support Jewish education.
David Yellin, the educator and scholar, is born in Jerusalem.
The Palestine Exploration Fund begins its surveys.
American settlers of the Adams colony arrive in Jaffa.
Mark Twain visits and describes a desolate land.
German Templers found a colony in Haifa.
Nahalat Shiva, a neighborhood of seven families, is founded in Jerusalem.
A pogrom in Odessa shakes the Jews of Russia.
German Templers found the Sarona colony near Jaffa.
Mea Shearim is founded in Jerusalem.
Naftali Herz Imber writes the poem that becomes Hatikvah.
Jews from Safed found Gei Oni, the first Rosh Pina.
Laurence Oliphant publishes The Land of Gilead and backs Jewish settlement.
About 25,000 Jews live in the land.

title: Zionism Takes Shape
intro: Pogroms in Russia set off the First Aliyah. Thinkers from Hess and Pinsker to Ahad Ha’am and Herzl turn the old longing for Zion into a political movement.
tp: Pogroms in Russia send thousands of Jews to the land.
Baron Edmond de Rothschild supports the new farming village.
After the pogroms the Odessa physician argues that Jews will never be accepted as equals and must win a land of their own.
Romanian and Polish Jews settle on the Carmel slope. Baron Rothschild supports the village and names it for his father James.
Romanian Jews settle at the Arab village of Jauna and build the first Jewish farming village in the Galilee. Rothschild begins to support it in 1884.
In This Is Not the Way he calls for a spiritual and cultural center in Zion rather than a state.
Eliezer Ben-Yehuda and the revival of Hebrew.
He arrives in 1881 and makes Hebrew the language of his home in Jerusalem. In 1890 he founds the Hebrew Language Committee.
He argues that antisemitism can end only with a Jewish state.
Herzl convenes it in Basel and calls for a Jewish homeland in the land of Israel.
also: Tsar Alexander II is assassinated and pogroms spread across Russia.
The student pioneers of BILU reach the land.
Itamar Ben-Avi, the first modern Hebrew-speaking child, is born in Jerusalem.
Russia’s May Laws restrict where Jews may live and work.
Yesud HaMa’ala is founded in the Hula Valley.
Ekron and Nes Ziona are founded.
The Lovers of Zion movement is founded to promote resettlement.
Gedera is founded by BILU settlers.
Rishon LeZion opens a Hebrew-language school.
Neve Tzedek is founded outside Jaffa.
Avshalom Feinberg, later a Nili spy, is born in Gedera.
Nathan Birnbaum coins the word Zionism.
Sarah Aaronsohn is born in Zikhron Yaakov.
Wine cellars open in Rishon LeZion.
The Ottomans bar Russian Jews from settling and buying land.
The railway from Jaffa to Jerusalem opens.
The Dreyfus Affair in France sharpens Zionist aims.
Esther Raab, the first Hebrew poet born in the land, is born in Petah Tikva.
Max Nordau speaks at the First Zionist Congress.
Herzl visits Jerusalem and meets Kaiser Wilhelm II.
The Jewish Colonial Trust is founded in London.
Sejera is founded in the Lower Galilee.

title: The 1900s
intro: The Second Aliyah begins, the first kibbutz is founded and Tel Aviv rises beside Jaffa. The Bezalel art school opens in Jerusalem.
tp: Britain offers land in East Africa after the Kishinev pogrom. The Zionist Congress debates it and rejects it in 1905.
Abraham Isaac Kook becomes rabbi of Jaffa and the farming villages and starts to bridge religious and secular Zionists.
Pogroms follow the failed revolution of 1905. They push Jews to the Second Aliyah and to America.
Jewish families found Tel Aviv beside Jaffa. The first kibbutz is founded at Degania.
also: About 50,000 Jews live in the land.
Rothschild transfers his colonies to the Jewish Colonization Association.
The Jewish National Fund is founded to buy land.
Kfar Tavor and Yavne’el are founded in the Galilee.
The Kishinev pogrom in Russia pushes more Jews to leave.
The Anglo-Palestine Bank opens in Jaffa.
The Second Aliyah begins and brings thousands of Jews from Eastern Europe.
Theodor Herzl dies in Austria at 44.
A. D. Gordon arrives and preaches the dignity of labor.
The family of the painter Nahum Gutman comes to the land.
The Herzliya Hebrew Gymnasium opens in Jaffa.
The Hapoel Hatzair labor party is founded.
The Seventh Zionist Congress rejects the Uganda Plan.
The Bezalel art school opens in Jerusalem.
Aaron Aaronsohn finds wild wheat near Rosh Pina.
A pogrom in Bialystok kills dozens.
Yitzhak Ben-Zvi arrives and joins Hashomer.
The Young Turk revolution restores the Ottoman constitution.
Arthur Ruppin opens the Palestine Office in Jaffa.
S. Y. Agnon arrives in Jaffa.
The first volume of Ben-Yehuda’s Hebrew dictionary appears.
The Hashomer watchmen’s group forms to guard Jewish farms.
Rachel Bluwstein arrives and later becomes a poet.
Yosef Haim Brenner arrives in Jaffa.
Sixty families draw lots for plots in Tel Aviv.

title: The 1910s
intro: The First World War ends Ottoman rule. Britain backs a Jewish national home in the Balfour Declaration and takes Jerusalem in December 1917.
tp: The painter comes to work at the Bezalel school. His drawings later record Jewish suffering in the First World War.
The Ottoman Empire enters the war on the German side.
Britain and France plan to divide the Ottoman Middle East between them.
Britain backs a Jewish national home, a goal that Chaim Weizmann pursued. British forces enter Jerusalem in December.
also: Ahuzat Bayit is renamed Tel Aviv.
The Atlit agricultural research station opens.
Meir Dizengoff becomes head of the Tel Aviv committee.
The cornerstone of the Technion is laid in Haifa.
Anna Ticho arrives in Jerusalem and later draws its hills.
Henrietta Szold founds Hadassah in New York.
The language war at the Technion settles on Hebrew.
Mendel Beilis is acquitted of blood libel in Kiev.
About 85,000 Jews live in the land.
The Ottoman Empire enters the war and expels Russian Jews.
The Zion Mule Corps forms in Egypt and serves at Gallipoli.
Moshe Dayan is born at Degania.
Hussein and McMahon begin their letters on Arab independence.
The Arab Revolt begins against the Ottomans.
British forces take Jerusalem in December, ending Ottoman rule.
The Ottomans expel the residents of Jaffa and Tel Aviv.
The Jewish Legion forms in the British army.
Sarah Aaronsohn dies after capture by the Ottomans.
The Zionist Commission arrives under Chaim Weizmann.
The cornerstone of the Hebrew University is laid.
Allenby wins the Battle of Megiddo.
Faisal and Weizmann sign an agreement.
Pogroms in Ukraine kill tens of thousands and push Jews to leave.

title: The 1920s
intro: Britain holds the Mandate. The Hebrew University opens on Mount Scopus, and the riots of 1929 end the Jewish community of Hebron.
tp: Joseph Trumpeldor and seven others die defending the Galilee outpost. His last words, said to be that it is good to die for our country, become a legend.
The League of Nations approves it. Transjordan is separated from the land west of the Jordan.
Reuven Rubin settles in Tel Aviv.
His bright landscapes help create a local style of painting.
About 67,000 Jews, many of them middle-class Poles, arrive after the United States closes its doors in 1924. They fill the towns, above all Tel Aviv.
In Hebron 67 Jews are killed on August 24 and the Jewish community leaves. Safed and Jerusalem are also attacked.
also: The San Remo conference assigns the Mandate for Palestine to Britain.
The Haganah is formed as a Jewish defense organization.
to 7 Riots in Jerusalem during the Nebi Musa festival kill five Jews.
Herbert Samuel arrives as the first High Commissioner.
The Histadrut labor federation is founded in Haifa.
Avraham Shlonsky arrives and begins to write modern Hebrew poetry.
Riots in Jaffa kill dozens of Jews and Arabs.
Haj Amin al-Husseini is named Mufti of Jerusalem.
Nahalal, the first moshav, is founded.
Yitzhak Rabin is born in Jerusalem.
The League of Nations confirms the Mandate.
Territory: Britain excludes Transjordan from the Jewish national home.
Jabotinsky founds the Betar youth movement.
The Mandate for Palestine takes effect.
The poet Haim Gouri is born in Tel Aviv.
The poet Hayim Nahman Bialik settles in Tel Aviv.
The Technion opens its first classes in Haifa.
Uri Zvi Greenberg arrives and writes in Hebrew.
The United States passes a law that sharply cuts Jewish immigration.
The Hebrew University opens on Mount Scopus.
Patrick Geddes plans the growth of Tel Aviv.
Brit Shalom, a group for Arab and Jewish understanding, is founded.
An economic crisis ends the Fourth Aliyah boom.
Unemployment and emigration peak in the economic crisis.
An earthquake kills hundreds in the land.
The Mandate recognizes the organized Jewish community.
Ariel Sharon is born in Kfar Malal.
A Yom Kippur dispute at the Western Wall inflames tensions.

title: The 1930s
intro: Immigration rises as the Nazis take power. The Arab Revolt begins in 1936, and the White Paper of 1939 limits Jewish immigration.
tp: A former Bauhaus student, he directs the Bezalel school from 1940.
More than 170,000 Jews flee Nazi Germany and Eastern Europe. Many are doctors, lawyers, musicians and architects.
It protests Jewish immigration and British policy and lasts until 1939.
Arab gunmen kill 19 Jews, 11 of them children, in the heart of the Arab Revolt.
Britain sharply limits Jewish immigration and land purchases as the Holocaust begins.
Six million Jews are murdered in Europe. Survivors seek refuge in the land.
also: Naomi Shemer is born at Kibbutz Kinneret.
The Passfield White Paper curbs Jewish immigration.
The Irgun, an armed underground group, is founded.
The Habima theater makes its home in Tel Aviv.
The poet Rachel dies in Tel Aviv.
The first Maccabiah games open in Tel Aviv.

tp: Zionist leaders meeting in New York call for a Jewish commonwealth after the war.
Jews of the land fight Nazi Germany in their own unit of the British army.

British forces seize the refugee ship off Haifa and send its 4,500 passengers back to Europe.
On November 29 the General Assembly votes for a Jewish state and an Arab state. The Jews accept and the Arabs reject.

to 2 A mob kills about 180 Jews in the Farhud in Baghdad.

title: Independence and Ingathering
intro: Israel declares independence, wins its first war and doubles its population in three years as Jews pour in from Europe and the Arab world.
tp: David Ben-Gurion declares independence and becomes prime minister of the provisional government. Five Arab armies attack on May 15.
Five Arab armies invade the day after independence. By the armistices of 1949 Israel holds more land than the partition plan gave it.
Armistice agreements with Egypt (Feb 24), Lebanon (Mar 23), Jordan (Apr 3) and Syria (Jul 20) end the War of Independence. Israel holds more land than the partition plan gave it.
In flights that began in 1949, the Yemenite Jewish airlift brings nearly 49,000 Jews from Yemen and Aden to Israel by September 1950.
Airlifts bring about 120,000 Jews from Iraq to Israel.
Every Jew has the right to immigrate to Israel and take citizenship.
Israel and West Germany sign in Luxembourg. Menachem Begin leads a violent protest outside the Knesset in January over the talks.
Israeli agents recruit Egyptian Jews for failed bombings in Egypt. Two are executed, and Defense Minister Pinhas Lavon resigns, with Ben-Gurion returning to the post.
also: The Israel Defense Forces are formed from the Haganah and other groups.
Chaim Weizmann is elected the first president.
Territory: Jordan annexes Judea and Samaria and East Jerusalem.
Jews arrive from Arab countries and Iran and reshape Israeli society.

The Free Officers coup in Egypt brings Nasser to power.
Yad Vashem is founded by law to remember the Holocaust.

Ben-Gurion resigns and moves to Sde Boker.

title: Sinai and the Years Between
intro: The Sinai Campaign opens a decade of quiet borders. Israel builds its water carrier and its institutions, tries Eichmann and makes peace with Germany.
tp: After Egypt nationalizes the Suez Canal, Israel, Britain and France plan the attack in secret at Sèvres. Israel takes Sinai in days. The United States and the Soviet Union force a withdrawal, completed in March 1957.
Israeli agents seize Adolf Eichmann in Argentina in 1960. He is tried in Jerusalem in 1961 and executed in 1962, the only death sentence Israel has carried out in a civil court.
A secret Mossad operation brings about 100,000 Jews from Morocco to Israel.
Levi Eshkol becomes prime minister as the founding generation begins to hand over power.
It brings water from the Sea of Galilee to the farms and towns of the south.
Twenty years after the Holocaust, the two countries exchange ambassadors.
S. Y. Agnon is the first Hebrew writer to receive the prize for literature.
also: Border police kill 48 Arab citizens at Kafr Qasim.
A UN emergency force deploys in Sinai and Gaza.
Thousands of Jews leave Egypt after the Sinai War.
Territory: Israel completes its withdrawal from Sinai and Gaza.
France agrees to help build the Dimona reactor.
Egypt and Syria merge into the United Arab Republic.
The Hebrew University opens its new campus at Givat Ram in Jerusalem.
Israel begins building the Dimona reactor.
A coup in Iraq and a crisis in Lebanon alarm Israel’s neighbors and its allies.
Riots break out in Haifa’s Wadi Salib over discrimination against Jews from North Africa.
Marc Chagall’s windows are dedicated at the Hadassah synagogue in Jerusalem.
Pope Paul VI makes the first papal visit to the Holy Land in modern times.
The Arab League founds the PLO.
Ephraim Kishon’s film Sallah Shabati is the first Israeli film nominated for an Academy Award.
Israeli spy Eli Cohen is hanged in Damascus.
The Israel Museum opens in Jerusalem, with the Shrine of the Book.
Military rule over Arab citizens of Israel ends.

title: The Six-Day War and Yom Kippur
intro: In six days Israel reunites Jerusalem and triples its territory. The War of Attrition, terror abroad and the shock of Yom Kippur follow.
tp: Israel takes Judea and Samaria, Gaza, Sinai, the Golan Heights and East Jerusalem. Jerusalem is united under Israeli control.
Israeli forces take the Old City, the Western Wall and the rest of Judea and Samaria, Sinai, Gaza and the Golan Heights.
Egypt shells Israeli positions along the Suez Canal and Israel answers with air raids deep in Egypt. The fighting is heaviest from March 1969 and a ceasefire takes hold on August 7, 1970.
The UN Security Council calls for Israeli withdrawal from territories and for peace and secure borders. Arab leaders had already declared three refusals at Khartoum.
She follows Levi Eshkol, who died in office on February 26. She resigns in April 1974 after the Yom Kippur War.
Palestinian terrorists kill 11 Israeli athletes and coaches at the Olympic Games.
Egypt and Syria attack on the holiest day of the year and Israel repels them. Ceasefires take hold on October 22 and 25.
Commandos fly to Uganda and rescue the hostages of a hijacked Air France plane. Yoni Netanyahu is killed leading the raid.
also: Egypt closes the Straits of Tiran to Israeli shipping.
Moshe Dayan becomes defense minister days before the Six-Day War.

Massacre at Lod Airport. Three Japanese gunmen working for a Palestinian group kill 26 people, most of them Puerto Rican pilgrims.
Territory: Israel and Egypt sign the first Sinai disengagement agreement.
Gunmen kill 18 people in Kiryat Shmona.
Massacre at Ma’alot. Gunmen seize a school in the north. Twenty-two schoolchildren are among the dead.

Yitzhak Rabin becomes prime minister for the first time.
A bomb in Jerusalem’s Zion Square kills 15.
Territory: the second Sinai agreement returns the Abu Rudeis oil fields and the passes.

title: Upheaval, Peace and Lebanon
intro: Begin’s victory ends Labor rule. Sadat comes to Jerusalem and Israel makes peace with Egypt, destroys Iraq’s reactor and goes to war in Lebanon.
tp: Likud wins the May 17 election and Menachem Begin becomes prime minister, ending three decades of Labor rule.
The Egyptian president addresses the Knesset and opens the way to peace.
The Camp David summit of September 1978 leads to the first peace treaty with an Arab state. Israel completes its return of Sinai on April 25, 1982.
Jets strike Iraq’s nuclear reactor near Baghdad before it can go into operation.
Israel invades to drive out the PLO, which leaves Beirut in August. Israel stays in southern Lebanon until 2000.
Thousands of Ethiopian Jews are brought to Israel by way of Sudan.
also: Zubin Mehta becomes music director of the Israel Philharmonic.
The Coastal Road massacre. Gunmen land from the sea, hijack a bus and kill 38 civilians, 13 of them children.
Israel wins the Eurovision Song Contest.
Summit: Begin and Sadat meet with President Carter at Camp David.
Menachem Begin shares the Nobel Peace Prize with Anwar Sadat.
Terrorists land by sea and attack Nahariya.

The Kahan Commission. It finds Ariel Sharon indirectly responsible for Sabra and Shatila, and he leaves the Defense Ministry.

Security forces arrest the Jewish Underground.

title: Intifada and the Great Aliyah
intro: The unity government tames inflation and pulls back to a security zone in Lebanon. The First Intifada erupts, Scuds fall in the Gulf War, and a million Jews begin to arrive from the Soviet Union.
tp: Israel pulls back to a strip of southern Lebanon, where it stays until 2000.
The unity government brings inflation of over 400 percent down within a year.
A Palestinian uprising begins in Gaza and spreads to Judea and Samaria. It lasts until 1993.
The Soviet Union opens its gates.
A mass aliyah begins that brings about a million Jews to Israel within a decade.
Scud missiles in the Gulf War.
Iraq fires about 40 missiles at Israeli cities. Israel does not respond.
About 14,000 Ethiopian Jews are flown to Israel in 36 hours.
Israel and its Arab neighbors open their first direct peace talks.
Labor wins the June election and Yitzhak Rabin becomes prime minister for the second time.
also: Israel frees 1,150 prisoners for three captured soldiers.
Israeli jets bomb PLO headquarters in Tunis.

intro: The Oslo Accords and peace with Jordan raise hopes. Rabin is murdered, the Camp David talks fail and the Second Intifada brings suicide bombings to Israel’s cities.
tp: Israel and the PLO sign the Declaration of Principles on the White House lawn. The Palestinian Authority is created.
Rabin and King Hussein sign the treaty and normalize relations.
A Jewish extremist shoots the prime minister after a peace rally in Tel Aviv. Shimon Peres takes over the same day.
Suicide bombers kill 45 people on Jerusalem buses in February and March.
Israel leaves the security zone in southern Lebanon after 18 years.
After the Camp David summit fails, a wave of suicide bombings and fighting lasts until 2005.
He beats Ehud Barak in the special election of February 6. He withdraws from Gaza in 2005, and a stroke ends his career in January 2006.

also: Israel and the Vatican sign the Fundamental Agreement.
Baruch Goldstein kills 29 worshippers in Hebron.

The Dolphinarium bombing. A suicide bomber kills 21 people outside a Tel Aviv discotheque, most of them teenagers.

tp: Israel removes all its soldiers and communities from the Strip.

Hundreds of thousands march over housing and the cost of living.

Operation Pillar of Defense in Gaza.

intro: The embassy moves to Jerusalem and the Abraham Accords bring peace with Gulf states. Five elections and the judicial protests divide Israel, and Hamas attacks on October 7.

The United Arab Emirates and Bahrain sign at the White House and normalize relations with Israel. Morocco and Sudan follow.
An 11-day war with Hamas sets off riots in mixed Arab and Jewish cities.

About 1,200 people are killed and about 250 are taken hostage. Israel launches the war in Gaza, Operation Swords of Iron.
also: Terrorists kill four at a Paris kosher supermarket.

Netta wins the Eurovision Song Contest.

Tel Aviv hosts the Eurovision Song Contest.

Operation Black Belt targets Islamic Jihad in Gaza.
Netanyahu and Benny Gantz form a unity government.
Benjamin Netanyahu returns as prime minister after the November 1 election.

intro: The day after the massacre, Israel is at war on seven fronts: Gaza, Lebanon, Syria, Judea and Samaria, Yemen, Iraq and Iran. Hezbollah’s leaders fall, Assad’s regime collapses, and a ceasefire brings the living hostages home.
tp: Hezbollah fires on the north the day after the massacre, and some 60,000 Israelis leave their homes.

Fighting that began on October 8, 2023 ends.
The Assad regime falls in Syria.
Israel moves to secure its Golan border.
Israel strikes Iran’s nuclear and missile sites, and the United States joins in.

also: The Houthis in Yemen launch their first missiles toward Israel.
